The project board — published by the pipeline, or served live.

## Uso

```bash
anchors board
```

## Subcomandos

### `anchors board serve`

Bring up the local board, with LIVE state instead of the pipeline snapshot.

```text
Brings the board up on a local server, reading the current state from GitHub.

The published board is a SNAPSHOT: the pipeline runs, generates the board.json, publishes. Between one
run and the next what you see is the past — and in a project with many agents delivering,
minutes are enough for the snapshot to lie about who has which card.

  anchors board serve                 # http://localhost:7777
  anchors board serve --port 8080
  anchors board serve --interval 15s  # the floor between two reads

HOW IT STAYS FRESH. The read is INCREMENTAL: it asks GitHub what changed
since the last time, and the cost follows the CHANGE instead of the time. When the incremental
is not available — on the first load, without permission, or with the API refusing — it
FALLS BACK to the full sweep (fallback), which re-reads everything.

The difference matters because of the rate limit: it is 5000 calls/hour shared among all
the project's agents, and a full sweep costs ~15. Reloading every 30s without
incremental would be 1800/hour from the board alone.

The --interval is the FLOOR between two reads, not the frequency: if nothing changed, it does not
re-read. It serves to keep the board from overloading the API when a lot happens at once.
```

#### Uso

```bash
anchors board serve [flags]
```

#### Flags

| Flag | Padrão | O que faz |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--interval` | `15s` | floor between two GitHub reads (not the frequency: with no change, it does not re-read) |
| `--port` | `7777` | local server port |
| `--repo` |  | owner/name (default: that of the current clone) |

## A fila de trabalho — família

Comandos da mesma família — o que distingue cada um:

| Comando | O que faz |
| --- | --- |
| [`anchors next`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/next/) | Pull and claim the next item from the queue (the worker calls this) |
| [`anchors queue`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/queue/) | List live tasks (the work the watcher queued) |
| [`anchors work`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/work/) | Emit the work prompt of a stage (spec\|code\|feature\|test\|review) for a target |
| [`anchors done`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/done/) | Close claimed task(s) (moves to the .anchors/done/ history) |
| [`anchors drop`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/drop/) | Discard a task from the queue without completing it (removes; does not archive) |
| [`anchors reclaim`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/reclaim/) | Return to the queue the tasks stuck in claimed (dead worker) |
| [`anchors deliver`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/deliver/) | Record the delivery of a stage — the review trigger |
| [`anchors decided`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/decided/) | Release the card `escalate --for-user` stopped, once the decision is made |
| [`anchors discard`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/discard/) | Take off the board the card that no longer makes sense, without deleting it |
| [`anchors unblock`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/unblock/) | Open the work card that unblocks a card stuck in `needs-user` |
| [`anchors escalate`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/escalate/) | Open the issue for a change needed in the plan or the spec |
| [`anchors report-bug`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/report-bug/) | Report a bug in Anchors itself at github.com/co2-lab/anchors |
| [`anchors synthesize`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/synthesize/) | Two PRs conflicting in CONTENT become a synthesis card |
| [`anchors watch`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/watch/) | The background watcher: sees changes and QUEUES work |
| [`anchors monitor`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/monitor/) | Watch the project's long processes: one line when one starts, stalls, dies or ends |
| [`anchors flow`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/flow/) | Operate the work flows (the puzzle of actions and results) |
| **`anchors board`** | The project board — published by the pipeline, or served live |
